A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original controller-synthesis experiments, ROA volumes, success rates, verification timings, and ablations, with further results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports Fossil 2.0 comparison results and observations about its failed certificates.

M1.justification: The two-stage training, Zubov-guided sampling, domain expansion, CEGIS refinement, and adaptive verification procedure remain unchanged. The loss equations displayed in v2 Section 3.1.1 were already present in v1 Appendix A.3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine dynamical systems spanning 2D to 12D, including both torque regimes for pendulum and path tracking. Fossil is evaluated on existing settings; the proposed future extensions are not tested.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Fossil 2.0 on Van der Pol, Double Integrator, and both pendulum torque settings. The existing DITL, Yang et al., Shi et al., and dReal comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes the 2D-quadrotor verification threshold from c2 = 0.20001 to 0.21 while retaining c1 = 0.2. Appendix C.1 also documents trajectory-based rejection of unsuccessful Fossil certificates in the newly added comparison.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 adds a qualitative failure analysis of Fossil, reporting claimed certificates whose controllers fail trajectory checks. The training ablations in Table 2 and their findings remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five runs with different seeds and use the same plus/minus variability reporting. The new checklist reiterates this practice without documenting additional runs, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds four Fossil results, including Double Integrator ROA 258.1 ± 36.3 with 80% success; existing methods' entries remain unchanged. Table 3 replaces the 2D-quadrotor timing of 209504 seconds with 104614 seconds under a changed threshold, so this is not a same-setting speedup. The distinct angular-state cartpole slice in Figure 7(f) is also removed.

T1.justification: Theorem 2.4 drops the general beta/psi/omega construction and retains its previously stated tanh special case. New Appendix B.2 supplies verification encodings, but Eq. (23) uses c2 for both exclusion thresholds, inconsistently with the c1-to-c2 band in Theorem 3.1. That theorem and its proof otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same training and verification contributions and the same headline ROA-volume and verification-speedup claims. The added comparison does not redefine those claims.

C2.justification: v2 attributes Fossil failures to a missing boundary condition and explains that poorer high-dimensional Zubov fitting motivates lowering the sampling threshold. The conclusion expands future directions to discrete/hybrid, time-varying, and perturbed systems while retaining the existing limitations on high-dimensional formal verification.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4 newly specifies sampling thresholds around 0.95, reduced toward 0.9 in higher dimensions. New Appendix C.7 identifies V100 GPUs with 16 GB for training and 5090 GPUs with 32 GB for verification. These are additional disclosures, not evidence of changed hardware or training settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds Fossil and its underlying framework, Z3, several certificate-learning references, and Clip-and-Verify, while dropping two general control-application references. The Fossil discussion extends the positioning against continuous-time methods, but the central novelty framing remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes local language edits, renames empirical verification schemes as evaluations, moves the full loss equations into the main text, and replaces numbered experiment subsections with paragraph headings. It also adds a verifier overview and the NeurIPS checklist while preserving the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: The document adopts the narrower NeurIPS layout, extensively rescaling and relocating figures, tables, and equations. Table 1 gains Fossil columns and an explicit evaluation-scheme column, with substantially smaller text. Figure 7(f) replaces the angular-state slice with the position/velocity slice already shown in Figure 2(c).

improvement.justification: The added continuous-time Fossil comparison and sampling/hardware disclosures modestly strengthen comparison relevance and reproducibility. Explicit evaluation labels also clarify which results have formal guarantees. These gains are tempered by smaller table text and the new threshold inconsistency in Eq. (23), although the main verification theorem and algorithm remain unchanged.
